summary: The Contrast ratio calculator is a free, no-sign-up other tool. Fill in the 32 fields it asks for and it works out contrast ratio (I know the color codes...) straight away, with the formula shown underneath. It is built for whatever you happen to be working on. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Contrast ratio calculator work?
sections.html:
The Contrast ratio calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports contrast ratio (I know the color codes...) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the color model, the type of text (I know the color codes...) and the type of text (I know the relative luminance...)); then you type in the H1 (I know the color codes...), the H1 (I know the color codes...), the H2 (I know the color codes...) and the H2 (I know the color codes...).

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

sections.title: The formula behind the Contrast ratio calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Contrast ratio=(((361 ÷ 5000) × (B1) + (447 ÷ 625) × (G1) + (1063 ÷ 5000) × (R1)), ((361 ÷ 5000) × (B2) + (447 ÷ 625) × (G2) + (1063 ÷ 5000) × (R2)))
Lighter color=((361 ÷ 5000) × (B1) + (447 ÷ 625) × (G1) + (1063 ÷ 5000) × (R1))
Darker color=((361 ÷ 5000) × (B2) + (447 ÷ 625) × (G2) + (1063 ÷ 5000) × (R2))
Contrast ratio=(lighter color, darker color)
Lighter color=(H1, S1, L1)
Darker color=(H2, S2, L2)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Contrast ratio calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Contrast ratio calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns contrast ratio (I know the color codes...). Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Contrast ratio calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for a few values, which is 32 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (4 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Contrast ratio calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. The calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.
